items.caption: Smoke Alarms.
items.excerpt: Smoke Alarms. Smoke alarms shall be installed and maintained in accordance with Sec. 34.907, MGO and with Wis. Admin. Code ch. SPS 362, Wis. Admin. Code § SPS 321.09 and Wis. Admin. Code § SPS 328.02 which are hereby incorporated by reference.

proposals.why: This is the only Chapter 27 provision on smoke alarms. It requires that smoke alarms be installed and maintained, but only 'in accordance with' other codes.
proposals.uncertainty: Chapter 27 does not itself say where alarms go, how many, or what counts as 'maintained'. Those rules are in MGO 34.907 and the SPS codes, which FixIt has not obtained or reviewed. Treating a covered or disabled alarm as 'not maintained' is an interpretation for an inspector.
proposals.decision: User: keep pending additional legal-source verification. Keep MGO 34.907, the Wisconsin smoke-alarm statutes (101.145, 101.645), the Wisconsin CO statutes (101.149, 101.647) and the SPS references separate; document overlaps and uncertainty; do not choose a governing rule without sufficient evidence. A 5-day written-notice repair deadline may be shown only when the applicable source and its conditions are established (design pending user review).

proposals.decision: PROVISIONAL: user accepted 27.07(2)(d) with the 27.03 definition of infestation (2026-11-14). Explain single-family vs other dwellings and the stated exceptions; a photo of possible droppings does not establish a sustained infestation; no claim that rentals must be entirely pest-free or that professional extermination is legally required. unresolved_discrepancies.issue: The egress rule says 'except as provided in Sec. 27.06(4), MGO', but 27.06(4) in this document (p. 29) is about habitable rooms below grade and says nothing about egress. Possibly an outdated cross-reference. Check the current official source; do not resolve it silently. INVESTIGATED 2026-11-14: identical wording on live Municode (Sep 1, 2026) and in the oldest structured version available (Feb 7, 2018); the rent-abatement schedule's exit row does not mention 27.06(4). The reason for the reference cannot be determined from the available official text and is not guessed. Next step: ask Building Inspection or obtain the amending ordinances (Ord. 9326, 1987; Ord. 12,349, 1999).
'Ord. 9326, 11-13-76' here; the same ordinance is dated '11-13-87' elsewhere in Chapter 27. Quoted as written; does not change the requirement.
Cites '29.19' for carbon monoxide detectors, but the current MGO 29.19 is 'Accrediting Standards and Tests'. CO appears in Chapter 29 only via 29.22 (adoption of SPS 328). Not interpreted.
Refers to 'sub. (2)(a)', 'sub. (2)(b)' and 'sub. (3)(h)' for alarm requirements that are now numbered (1)(b)1./(1)(b)2. Not interpreted.

Chapter 27 says handrails and guardrails are 'as specified in Wis. Admin. Code § SPS 321.04(2) or ch. SPS 362'. In the current SPS 321.04 (read on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov 2026-11-14), sub. (2) is 'Details' (width, riser height, tread depth, headroom); handrails and guards are in sub. (3) 'Handrails and guards' (e.g. (3)(a)1.: 'A flight of stairs with more than 3 risers shall be provided with at least one handrail for the full length of the flight.'). 27.05(2)(i) cites SPS 321.04 without a subsection. Possibly an outdated cross-reference; not interpreted. SPS 321 applies by its own terms to 1-2 family dwellings begun on or after June 1, 1980 (SPS 320.03, 320.04(1)(a), 320.05(1)); whether Chapter 27's incorporation extends it to other buildings is not determined.

Chapter 27 incorporates 'Wis. Admin. Code § SPS 328.02' for smoke alarms. The current SPS 328.02 is 'Scope' (created CR 10-089, eff. 2-1-11); smoke detectors are now SPS 328.03 ('renum. from Comm 28.02 ... eff. 2-1-11'). Probably not updated after the 2011 renumbering; not interpreted.

The pest rule distinguishes 'a single-family dwelling' from 'any residential dwelling other than a single-family dwelling', but 27.03 does not define 'single-family dwelling' (it defines 'Dwelling' and lists 'Single-family detached dwellings' as a type of residential building). How a rented single-family house, or one shared by unrelated tenants, is classified is not determined.

The statute page's editorial note says 'See also ss. SPS 321.095 and 366.1010 (2)'. The current SPS 321.095 is 'Automatic fire sprinklers'; CO detectors in the Uniform Dwelling Code are SPS 321.097. Editorial note only; not interpreted.
